summary: EMILDAI is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in law, data and artificial intelligence, coordinated by Dublin City University with Avignon, Erasmus University Rotterdam, Fundação Getulio Vargas in Rio, León and Pisa. It offers up to 12 full scholarships with €1,400 a month and 10 fee waivers. There is no application fee. Round 1 runs from 16 November 2026 to 17 January 2027.
meta_title: EMILDAI 2027: Erasmus Mundus law, data and AI scholarship
meta_description: EMILDAI gives up to 12 full scholarships with €1,400 a month and 10 fee waivers for a law, data and AI master's from Dublin. Round 1 closes 17 January 2027.
covers: Full scholarship (up to 12): all tuition plus €1,400 a month for 24 months.
Full fee waiver (up to 6): tuition for both years, no deposit, no allowance.
Partial fee waiver (up to 4): second-year tuition only.
Self-funded non-EU students pay €20,919 a year.
eligibility: Applicants of every nationality, with no more than 10% of the class from one nationality.
Law stream: normally an upper second (2:1) or equivalent in law, or a degree with law as a significant part. Computing stream: a lower second (2:2) or equivalent in computing.
English at C1 (IELTS 6.5 or equivalent), or proof such as a previous degree taught in English. A medium-of-instruction letter is accepted only from a country whose official first language is English.
Tracks A and B also need French or Spanish; tracks C and D are taught only in English.
how_to_apply: Apply in round 1, from 16 November 2026 to 17 January 2027. The portal does not accept applications after the deadline.
Upload your diplomas and transcripts (with certified English translations), language evidence, your stream and track choice, a personal statement of 500 to 750 words, a CV and two reference letters.
Applications are scored on academic merit (70%), professional experience (20%) and the personal statement (10%). Results come in March 2027.
Round 2, from 21 March to 28 May 2027, is for self-funded applicants only.
watch_out: Ghana's official language is English, so a medium-of-instruction letter from a Ghanaian university should count; ask the programme to confirm before relying on it.
Self-funded and partial-waiver students pay a deposit (the programme's pages give €500 and €750).

faq.q: When is the EMILDAI scholarship deadline?
faq.a: Round 1 closes on 17 January 2027. It opens on 16 November 2026.

faq.q: Can computer science graduates apply to EMILDAI?
faq.a: Yes. The computing stream asks for a 2:2 or equivalent in computing; the law stream asks for a 2:1 in law.
